{{Quote|Oh, I'm just an old man. Used to be on the Royal Council. Traveled, wrote a lot of books. The Galactic Phrasebook, that was mine.|Ebenn Q3 Baobab to a spacer|<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>}}
The '''''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide''''' was a [[Book/Legends|book]] written by the [[Human/Legends|Human]] scholar and polymath [[Ebenn Q3 Baobab/Legends|Ebenn Q3 Baobab]]. That book was designed for use by other Humans and provided them with simple phrases in several [[Language/Legends|languages]] other than [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]]. Published by [[Baobab Publishing/Legends|Baobab Publishing]], the ''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'' was first released in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], and a new edition was issued in [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]], twenty-eight [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later.

==History==
{{Quote|A must have when travelling without your protocol droid!|Extract from the book's back cover|<ref name="GPBTG" />}}
The ''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'' was the ''magnum opus'' of [[Ebenn Q3 Baobab/Legends|Ebenn Q3 Baobab]], a famous [[Manda/Legends|Manda]]-born [[Human/Legends|Human]] polymath. A first version of that book was released by [[Baobab Publishing/Legends|Baobab Publishing]]<ref name="SPL" /> prior to the fourth [[Standard month/Legends|month]]<ref name="HNN51">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|51|life/13411_1.html|Today's Traveler - The Art of Dealing with Snivvians}}</ref> of the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="SPL" /> Shortly before the subsequent [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|outbreak]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Baobab wrote a supplement to his seminal phrase [[Book/Legends|book]], which pertained to the language of the [[Snivvian/Legends|Snivvians]], an art-inclined [[Species/Legends|species]] from [[Cadomai Prime/Legends|Cadomai Prime]]. The supplement was then made available in the [[HoloNet News Vol. 531 51|fifty-first issue]] of the 531st [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] volume, under the title of "Today's Traveler - The Art of Dealing with Snivvians."<ref name="HNN51" /> In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], about eight months after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the young [[Tash Arranda/Legends|Tash Arranda]] consulted Baobab's book while redacting ''[[Death in the Slave Pits of Lorrd, Or: What I Did On My Inter-Term Break]]'', an essay recounting a visit she made to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Lorrd/Legends|Lorrd]] with her adopted uncle, the [[Senior Anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]].<ref name="SPL" /> [[6 ABY/Legends|Six years later]], a new version of the ''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'' was published,<ref name="GPBTG" /> while Baobab himself had been retired and suffering from severe dementia for a few years.<ref name="SWG" />

==Content==
{{Quote|From the restaurant server who anticipates an imminent need for napkins to the improvisational street performer capable of imitating hundreds of species, Lorrdians are capable of responding to your every expression and they are sure to make your visit to Lorrd a delight. As long as you don't play sabacc with them, that is.|Extract from the first edition|<ref name="SPL" />}}
The first edition notably included a chapter pertaining to the [[Lorrdian/Legends|Lorrdians]], a group of culturally unique Humans from the planet Lorrd in the [[Kanz sector/Legends|Kanz sector]]. The bibliographic reference for that edition was properly written as: "Baobab, Ebenn Q3. ''Galactic Phrasebook and Travel Guide''. Manda: Baobab Publishing, (13 GrS)."<ref name="SPL" /> The 6 ABY edition included a rather brief travel guide, offering general advice and a glimpse at [[Cantina/Legends|cantinas]], [[Hotel/Legends|hotels]], [[Sauna/Legends|saunas]], and other such facilities in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]], a large [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. The conversation guide itself contained sections on [[Bocce/Legends|Bocce]], [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]], [[Ewokese/Legends|Ewokese]], [[Binary/Legends|Binary]], [[Shyriiwook/Legends|Shyriiwook]], [[Jawaese/Legends|Jawaese]], [[Tusken/Legends|Tusken]], [[Old Gungan/Legends|Old Gungan]], [[Pak Pak/Legends|Neimoidian]] and [[Sullustese/Legends|Sullustese]]. In addition to its purely linguistic content, the guide also advised on how to deal with the native speakers of those languages. The most common&mdash;and potentially problematic&mdash;situations were covered, such as how to face off with a [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raider]], how to shoo bothersome droids, or how to avoid tasting less-than-engaging Gungan food. The whole book was illustrated throughout with lighthearted drawings, often representing a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] in humorous situations.<ref name="GPBTG" />

==Behind the scenes==
The ''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'' first appeared in [[2001]], in the form of its [[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|real-world equivalent]], written by ''Star Wars'' sound designer [[Ben Burtt]].<ref name="GPBTG" /> The defunct [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|MMORPG]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' stated that Baobab had already published his ''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'' before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], during which the game was set.<ref name="SWG" /> This stood as a continuity error, since the real-world book stated that it was published 6 ABY.<ref name="GPBTG" /> However, the Volume 531, Issue 51 of the [[HoloNet News (original website)|HoloNet News website]] showed that a version of that tome was in existence around one month before the Clone Wars.<ref name="HNN51" /> ''[[Death in the Slave Pits of Lorrd]]'', an in-universe story written by [[Adrick Tolliver]] for the defunct [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] subscriber feature of [[StarWars.com]], confirmed that the book was originally published in 13 [[Great ReSynchronization|GrS]]&mdash;that is, 22 BBY.<ref name="SPL" />
